event_info.event_description: Analyze for disclosures on global pandemic risks. Look for corporate language discussing widespread impacts like supply chain disruptions, labor shortages, remote work transitions, and fundamental shifts in consumer demand.

holistic_analysis: Bristol-Myers Squibb’s 2022 Form 10-K identifies COVID-19 primarily as a continuing, multi-faceted operational risk rather than an existential financial crisis.  The filing, delivered less than three years after the WHO pandemic declaration, discusses both experienced impacts (e.g., lower patient starts; heightened cyber-attacks) and a suite of forward-looking exposures—supply-chain bottlenecks, raw-material scarcity, labor shortages, counterfeit-drug proliferation, clinical-trial delays.  The language is mostly qualitative but uses strong phrases such as “materially impact,” signalling management views the hazard as significant.  Mitigating language is present (“we did not experience significant manufacturing issues”), but is outweighed by acknowledgements that similar or worse effects could recur.  Under the Time Decay Principle, COVID-19 remains a “recent” event, so individual sentence scores can range as high as 10, yet the absence of quantified dollar impacts tempers severity.  Overall, the pandemic is framed as an ongoing, moderate-to-high operational risk, with particular sensitivity in supply continuity and demand fluctuations, justifying mid-range snippet scores that peak around 5–6.
